notes: Self-declared open-world action RPG and every system under it is RPG - levels, skill points, a branching tree, quest boards, a boss ladder - so RPG leads alone; the skill's own worked example takes 'Open-world Action RPG' to RPG rather than splitting Action out, and the Action RPG preset already carries the combat framing. Shape is world-hub-dungeon because the two answers together describe exactly that: eight zones as one continuous overworld with the Starting Village named as the hub, and the Spider Caves and Endgame Fortress instanced per party, so the P4 is stated rather than estimated and stands, with P3 on the overworld-to-instance transition and the shops, forge and Butterfly Mansion you go inside. Added gate-progression for the stated zone unlocks and level-and-yen breathing gates, collectible-nodes for the ore and demon-horn gathering behind the forge's crafting, npc-population for the townsfolk who work by day and hide at night, and terrain-relief for the alpine pass and summit, whose tiered cost is the only elevation claim I make. I judged the mountain trainer cave and the twisting Spider tunnels not to earn a P2, since one is a single interior off a hillside and the other is inside an instanced map rather than layered over the overworld, and the tutorial obby is a teaching space rather than a second genre.
